llm.reply:
NCBIGene:1029, name: cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 2A is associated with Li-Fraumeni syndrome in the retrieved answer set [1]. NCBIGene:11200, name: checkpoint kinase 2 is also associated with the syndrome in that set [3]. NCBIGene:7157, name: tumor protein p53 is the third associated gene [4].

## Causal evidence

The supporting literature specifically describes Li-Fraumeni syndrome as a cancer predisposition syndrome caused by a germline TP53 mutation [19: "a cancer predisposition syndrome caused by a germline mutation of the TP53 gene"]. Its inheritance is autosomal dominant with high penetrance [19: "It has an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance with high penetrance"]. The mechanistic description links TP53 mutations to loss of p53 function [19: "In LFS, TP53 gene mutations cause the loss of function of p53"].

## Phenotypic variability

Clinical heterogeneity occurs between families carrying the same pathogenic TP53 variant and within individual families [22: "Phenotypic heterogeneity is present among different families affected by the same pathogenic variant in TP53 gene and among members of the same family"]. Possible contributors include variation in TP53 or related genes, copy-number variation, and epigenetic deregulation, but these are presented as potential explanations rather than established determinants [22: "polymorphic variants in TP53 gene or in TP53-related genes, copy number variations in particular regions, and/or epigenetic deregulation of TP53 expression might be responsible for clinical heterogeneity"].

Genes associated with Li-Fraumeni syndrome include NCBIGene:1029, named cyclin dependent kinase inhibitor 2A [1]. They also include NCBIGene:11200, named checkpoint kinase 2 [3]. The third gene is NCBIGene:7157, named tumor protein p53 [4].

## Disease and mechanism

The disease name is Li-Fraumeni syndrome [2]. The literature describes germline TP53 mutation as causing the cancer predisposition syndrome [19: "a cancer predisposition syndrome caused by a germline mutation of the TP53 gene"]. Clinical heterogeneity occurs even within families [22: "Phenotypic heterogeneity is present among different families affected by the same pathogenic variant in TP53 gene and among members of the same family"]. Multidisciplinary management is recommended [21: "The diagnosis and management of Li-Fraumeni syndrome should be performed by a multidisciplinary team"].
